content: The Ateneo School of Medicine and Public Health (ASMPH) is the medical school of Ateneo de Manila University, a private Roman Catholic university operated by the Society of Jesus in the Philippines. The school is situated within the Eugenio Lopez III Medical Complex in Ortigas Center, Pasig City, adjacent to its partner hospital, The Medical City. The academic program at ASMPH leverages the combined expertise and resources of the Loyola Schools, the Health Unit of the Ateneo Graduate School of Business, and its partner training hospital, The Medical City. The program includes a pre-professional phase, which is integrated with the Health Sciences program of the School of Science and Engineering at the Loyola Schools. It is also compatible with other degree programs, such as majors in Biology, Psychology, Chemistry, Physics, Medical Technology, Zoology, Economics, Interdisciplinary Studies, and others from various schools and universities. The professional phase of the program is a dual-degree offering that culminates in the conferral of both a Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree and a Master of Management (MM) degree. The Dean of ASMPH is Dr. A. A. Serving as Associate Dean is Dr. Maria Eufemia C. Sc. Dr. Yap earned her Bachelor of Science degree in Biology from Ateneo in 1983. She completed her medical studies at the Far Eastern University Nicanor Reyes Medical Foundation in 1987. She later pursued a Master of Science in Community Health and Health Management at the University of Heidelberg, graduating in 1997. Dr. Yap has held various positions in Ateneo’s health-related initiatives, including the Center for Community Services (CCS) and the Health Alternatives for Total Human Development Institute (HEALTHDEV). She subsequently joined the Ateneo Graduate School of Business (AGSB) as a faculty member, later becoming Associate Director and Assistant to the Vice President for the Professional Schools. Since 2003, she has served as the Director of the AGSB's Health Unit. Dr. Ma. Luz S., FPPA, has been appointed as the Director for Academic Affairs and Faculty Development. She earned her Bachelor of Arts in Psychology in 1981 and her Doctor of Medicine degree from the University of the Philippines in 1987. She obtained a Diplomate from the Philippine Board of Psychiatry in 1999. Before her current role, Dr. Querubin was an attending psychiatrist in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Medicine at the Philippine General Hospital. She is currently a member of the medical staff in the Department of Psychiatry at The Medical City. Dr. Querubin has also served as an Associate Clinical Professor at the College of Medicine, University of the Philippines, a faculty member for Ateneo’s Leaders for Health Program, and a Senior Lecturer in the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Melbourne.
